# Orthographic Studio

> Describe a 3D scene as flat outlines in three orthographic views (front, top, right side), traced over reference images, and check the result through a perspective camera. Each object's solid is the intersection of its three outlines extruded along their view directions. Built to be driven by LLM agents: one JSON document format, a validator that reports every problem with a JSON Pointer, and renders of every view for visual self-checks.

- Editor: https://3d.tris.sh/orthographic/
- MCP server: https://3d.tris.sh/orthographic/mcp (Streamable HTTP, no auth)
- JSON Schema: https://3d.tris.sh/orthographic/schema.json
- HTTP API index: https://3d.tris.sh/orthographic/api

No browser is needed: everything the editor does is available as tools, over MCP or plain HTTP.

## Connecting

- Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http orthographic https://3d.tris.sh/orthographic/mcp`
- Claude.ai or ChatGPT: add a custom connector with the URL `https://3d.tris.sh/orthographic/mcp` (no authentication).
- Any HTTP client: `POST https://3d.tris.sh/orthographic/api/tools/{tool}` with the tool's arguments as a JSON body; `GET https://3d.tris.sh/orthographic/api/tools` lists the tools with their JSON Schemas.

## Scenes and tools

The server stores scenes. `create_scene` returns a `sceneId` and an `editorUrl`; every other tool takes the `sceneId` (or the `editorUrl` itself). Give the `editorUrl` to the person you are working with: the editor at that link shows the scene live, and their edits there are visible to your next call. A person can also start in the editor and press Share, then give you the link.

Anyone with a scene's id can read and edit it, so treat the link as the access key. Scenes unedited for 90 days are deleted.

Every tool answers `{ ok, issues, ... }` and never throws; `ok` is false when an issue is an error, and then nothing changed. Every edit is one undoable step, reports the new `revision`, and returns the objects it touched (with derived bounds) and their geometry problems.

| Tool | Does |
|------|------|
| `read_guide` | This guide (`schema: true` adds the JSON Schema). |
| `create_scene` | A new scene, empty or from `document`. |
| `get_scene` | The scene as a document (images listed without pixels). |
| `load_document` | Replace the whole scene with a document: the fastest way to write many objects. |
| `validate` | Every problem in a scene or a `document`, with JSON Pointer paths, geometry included. |
| `add_image` | A reference image from a public `url` or base64 `data`; returns its id and pixel size. |
| `add_object` | An object from world-unit `outlines`, or a `primitive` (`box`, `ellipsoid`, `cylinder`, `rock`) filling `center` ± `size` / 2. |
| `update_object` | Name, kind, color, visible, locked, reviewed, opacity, notes. |
| `set_outline` | Replace one view's outline (world units). |
| `set_bounds` | Set any of min/max per axis for objects or a group; outlines scale. |
| `move_objects`, `duplicate_objects`, `delete_objects` | As named; offsets are `{x, y, z}`. |
| `set_scene` | Title, frame `size`, `metersPerUnit`, notes. |
| `set_camera` | Position, target, lens (`verticalFovDegrees` or `focalLengthMm35Equivalent`), roll, near, far, frame, locked. |
| `set_display` | Perspective drawing style, grid, labels, crosshair. |
| `set_reference` | Put an image behind a view, move it, or `remove: true`. |
| `undo`, `redo` | One shared history for agents and the editor. |
| `render` | PNGs of `front`, `top`, `side`, `perspective` (as images over MCP, data URLs over HTTP) plus links to them. |
| `export` | Links to `scene.json`, `agent.json`, `objects.csv`, `views.svg`, `editor.html` (the editor with the scene inside, one offline file). |

## Coordinates

- Right-handed, Z up, one scene unit (u) per unit. `scene.metersPerUnit` records a real-world scale, or null.
- X is right in the front view, Y is depth away from the front camera, Z is up.
- The scene frame is the box from (0, 0, 0) to `scene.size`. It is a drawing guide, not a boundary.

| View | Looks along | Point order | Horizontal | Vertical |
|------|-------------|-------------|------------|----------|
| `front` | +Y | `[x, z]` | x (right) | z (up) |
| `top` | −Z (down) | `[x, y]` | x (right) | y (away from the front camera) |
| `side` | −X (the right side) | `[y, z]` | y (right) | z (up) |

## How a solid is made

An object has exactly one outline per view: a simple closed polygon in world units, 3–512 points, no repeated closing point, no self-intersections, no holes. The solid is every point (x, y, z) whose front projection (x, z), top projection (x, y) and side projection (y, z) all fall inside their outlines.

Consequences worth planning for:

- Views share axes: front and top share x, top and side share y, front and side share z. Both views of an axis should span the same range; if they do not, the box uses the union and the narrower outline clips the solid (`extent-mismatch` warning).
- The outlines must agree on where the object is thick and thin. If the front says the top is narrow and the side says the top is wide, the solid is narrow there and the side outline is not filled (`low-coverage` warning, per view). If they share no volume at all, there is no solid (`no-common-volume` error).
- Concave detail survives only when every view allows it. A hole through an object cannot be represented; split it into several objects instead.
- Anything the three silhouettes cannot capture (a dent seen from no axis) is not captured. Prefer several simple objects over one complicated one.

## The document

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://3d.tris.sh/orthographic/schema.json",
  "format": "orthographic-scene",
  "version": 1,
  "scene": { "title": "Cave entrance", "size": { "x": 40, "y": 30, "z": 20 }, "metersPerUnit": null },
  "objects": [
    {
      "id": "pillar",
      "name": "Stone pillar",
      "kind": "rock",
      "color": "#efc875",
      "outlines": {
        "front": [[8, 2], [12, 2], [11, 16], [9, 16]],
        "top": [[8, 8], [12, 8], [12, 12], [8, 12]],
        "side": [[8, 2], [12, 2], [11, 16], [9, 16]]
      }
    }
  ],
  "camera": {
    "position": { "x": 20, "y": -30, "z": 12 },
    "target": { "x": 20, "y": 15, "z": 8 },
    "focalLengthMm35Equivalent": 35,
    "frame": { "width": 1600, "height": 900 }
  },
  "references": {
    "front": { "image": "photo", "opacity": 0.6, "min": { "x": 0, "z": 0 }, "size": { "x": 40, "z": 22.5 } },
    "perspective": { "image": "photo", "opacity": 0.5 }
  },
  "images": {
    "photo": { "name": "entrance.jpg", "mimeType": "image/jpeg", "width": 1600, "height": 900, "data": "<base64>" }
  }
}
```

Required: `format`, `version`, `scene.size`, `objects` (each with `id` and `outlines`). Everything else has defaults.

- `objects[].id`: letters, digits, `_ . -`, starting with a letter or digit, unique. `name`, `kind` (free tag), `color` (`#rrggbb`), `visible`, `locked`, `reviewed`, `opacity` (0.05–1, below 1 renders translucent), `notes`.
- `camera`: `position`, `target`, and the lens as `verticalFovDegrees` (5–140) or `focalLengthMm35Equivalent` (f = 12 mm / tan(vertical FOV / 2); if both are given they must agree), plus `rollDegrees`, `near`, `far`, `frame` (pixels, fixes the aspect ratio).
- `references`: one optional image per view. `front`/`top`/`side` place the image on the view plane: its lower-left corner at `min`, stretched to `size`, both named by that view's axes (`{x, z}` for front, `{x, y}` for top, `{y, z}` for side). Image right is the view's horizontal axis, image up its vertical axis. `perspective` is a screen overlay on the camera frame: `offsetPercent {x, y}`, `scale` (1 fits the frame), `rotationDegrees`, `blend`.
- `images`: keyed by id. `data` is the base64 file (PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF). It may be omitted only when the editor already holds that image.
- Documents the editor writes also contain `derived` blocks (bounds, center, size, camera matrices), `display`, `reconstruction`, `editor` and `meshCache`. They are read-only or optional; `derived` is ignored on load.

## Workflow for turning an image into a scene

1. `create_scene`, and share its `editorUrl`.
2. Decide the scene frame from the image (for a front-facing photo: width = x, height = z, pick a plausible depth y) with `set_scene`, including `metersPerUnit` if a scale is known.
3. `add_image`, then `set_reference` on the front view (without `min`/`size` it is fitted to the frame) and, if the camera is known, on the perspective view too.
4. For each object, trace its front outline in x/z from the image, then invent consistent top (x/y) and side (y/z) outlines: reuse the front's x range in top and its z range in side. Use `add_object` per object, or write them all with `load_document`.
5. `validate`. Fix every error; read every warning.
6. `render` the views and compare them with the references. Adjust outlines, the camera (position, target, focal length) or the reference placement, then repeat from 5.

## HTTP API

All endpoints accept and return JSON (CORS is open). Errors come back as `{ "ok": false, "issues": [...] }`. Besides the tools (`/api/tools/{tool}`), a few endpoints take a whole document and store nothing:

- `POST /orthographic/api/validate`: body is a document. Returns `{ ok, issues }`, including the geometry checks (reconstructs every solid).
- `POST /orthographic/api/render`: body `{ document, views?, width?, height?, references?, labels?, grid? }`. `views` defaults to all of `front`, `top`, `side`, `perspective`. Orthographic views are fitted to the scene at `width` × `height` (default 1200 × 900); perspective uses the camera frame (`width` scales it). References are drawn whenever assigned, unless `references` is false. Returns `{ ok, issues, images: { view: "data:image/png;base64,…" } }`.
- `POST /orthographic/api/render/{front|top|side|perspective}.png`: body is a document; returns the PNG itself. Query: `width`, `height`, `references=false`. Issues are in the `X-Issues` header (URL-encoded JSON).

```sh
curl -s -X POST --data-binary @scene.json https://3d.tris.sh/orthographic/api/validate
curl -s -X POST --data-binary @scene.json https://3d.tris.sh/orthographic/api/render/front.png -o front.png
```

Renders run one at a time; a busy server answers 503 with `Retry-After`.

Stored scenes also have plain GET links, handy for tools that can only fetch pages:

- `GET /orthographic/api/scenes/{id}`: `{ sceneId, revision, editorUrl, document }`.
- `GET /orthographic/api/scenes/{id}/render/{front|top|side|perspective}.png`: a render (query: `width`, `height`, `references`, `labels`, `grid`).
- `GET /orthographic/api/scenes/{id}/export/{scene.json|agent.json|objects.csv|views.svg|editor.html}`: downloads.

## In the page: `window.orthographic`

For agents that already drive a browser; the tools above do the same without one. Calls return `{ ok, issues, ... }` (edits, checks and renders as promises) and never throw. Edits use the document's shapes (`{x, y, z}` objects, world-unit outline points), apply as one undoable step, and change nothing when an issue is an error.

- `getDocument({ images: "metadata" | "data" | "none", derived, editor })` → the document (synchronous).
- `loadDocument(doc)`, `validate(doc?)` (no argument: the current scene, geometry included), `waitForGeometry()`.
- `addImage({ data, name })` → `{ id }` (base64 or a data: URL; the id is a hash of the bytes).
- `addObject({ id?, name, kind, color, outlines })` or `addObject({ primitive: "box" | "ellipsoid" | "cylinder" | "rock", center, size })` → `{ id }`.
- `updateObject(id, { name, kind, color, visible, locked, reviewed, opacity, notes })`, `setOutline(id, view, points)`, `setBounds(idOrIds, { min: {x,y,z}, max: {x,y,z} })` (any subset of axes; outlines scale), `moveObjects(ids, {x,y,z})`, `duplicateObjects(ids, offset?)`, `deleteObjects(ids)`.
- `setScene({ title, size, metersPerUnit, notes })`, `setCamera({ position, target, verticalFovDegrees | focalLengthMm35Equivalent, rollDegrees, near, far, frame, locked })`, `setDisplay({ style, grid, labels, crosshair })`.
- `setReference(view, { image, opacity, visible, min, size } | null)` for `front`/`top`/`side`; `setReference("perspective", { image, opacity, visible, offsetPercent, scale, rotationDegrees, blend } | null)`.
- `render({ views, width, height, references, labels, grid, format: "png" | "svg" })` → `{ images }`; `sheet()` → `{ svg }` (the three views on one drawing).
- `select(ids)`, `undo()`, `redo()`.

## Issues

Each issue is `{ severity: "error" | "warning", code, path, message, objectId?, view? }`; `path` is a JSON Pointer into the document. Common codes:

- `schema-*`: the document does not match the schema (`schema-additionalProperties` names the unknown key).
- `ring-self-intersection`, `ring-repeated-point`, `ring-too-few-points`, `ring-too-many-points`, `ring-zero-area`, `ring-not-finite`: an outline is not a simple polygon.
- `duplicate-id`, `collapsed-axis` (an object thinner than 0.001 u), `unknown-image`, `image-without-data`, `invalid-camera`, `camera-lens-mismatch`.
- `extent-mismatch` (warning): two views disagree on a shared axis.
- `no-common-volume` (error) and `low-coverage` (warning): the outlines do not describe one consistent solid.
- `outside-frame` (warning): an object extends past the scene frame.
- `argument-*`: a tool's arguments do not match its schema (`argument-additionalProperties` names the unknown argument).
- `unknown-scene`, `unknown-object`, `unknown-image`, `object-locked`, `revision-conflict` (a save based on an old revision).
- `invalid-url`, `fetch-failed`, `invalid-image`, `image-too-large`: `add_image` could not use the image.
- `busy`: the renderer has a queue; retry in a few seconds.
